extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, DHS adjudicators, consular officers, policymakers, and members of the public affected by public charge rules (applicants for admission or adjustment of status)
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule text defining DHS's implementation of the public charge ground of inadmissibility, including definitions, factors for determinations, exemptions/waivers, bond provisions, and required administrative analyses (NEPA, PRA, federalism, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: SBREFA / Major rule designation and effective-date constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Management and Budget has designated this final rule as a major rule as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804; the rule likely will result in an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or otherwise meet the major rule thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, absent exceptional circumstances, this final rule must be effective no earlier than 60 days after the date on which Congress receives a report submitted by DHS as required by 5 U.S.C. 801(a)(1). This final rule will be effective December 23, 2022, which meets this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must assess whether the rule has substantial direct effects on States, or on Federal-State relationships, or on distribution of power among levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS determined this final rule would not have substantial direct effects on the States or preempt State law, and thus does not have sufficient federalism implications to warrant a federalism summary impact statement (in accordance with section 6 of E.O. 13132).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12988 (Civil Justice Reform) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules must be drafted and reviewed to provide a clear legal standard and to eliminate drafting errors and ambiguities to minimize litigation and burden on courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This final rule was drafted and reviewed in accordance with E.O. 12988; DHS has determined that it meets the applicable standards provided in section 3 of E.O. 12988.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 (Tribal consultation) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must determine whether rule has 'tribal implications'—substantial direct effects on Indian Tribes or on Federal-Tribal relationships or distribution of power between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS determined this final rule does not have tribal implications and thus requires no further agency action or analysis under E.O. 13175.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Policymaking Assessment criteria (Sec. 654, Treasury & General Government Appropriations Act, 1999)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rule may affect family well-being, agencies must assess specified family impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must assess whether the regulatory action: (1) impacts family stability or safety (marital commitment); (2) impacts parental authority in education/nurture/supervision; (3) helps the family perform its functions; (4) affects disposable income or poverty of families and children; (5) financially impacts families only to the extent justified; (6) may be carried out by State/local government or by the family; and (7) establishes a policy concerning youth behavior/personal responsibility relative to societal norms. If affirmative, prepare an impact assessment addressing statutory criteria. DHS determined this rule does not affect family well-being and is not issuing an assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA categorical exclusion conditions (DHS Instruction Manual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under DHS NEPA procedures, for an action to be categorically excluded it must satisfy three specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An action must: (1) clearly fit within one or more categorical exclusions; (2) not be a piece of a larger action; and (3) have no extraordinary circumstances creating potential for a significant environmental effect. DHS determined this final rule fits within Categorical Exclusion A3(d) because it interprets or amends a regulation without changing its environmental effect; therefore no further NEPA analysis is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) obligations and information-collection notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, DHS must submit reporting requirements for OMB review unless exempt; the rule includes an information-collection notice and invites public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS invited written comments and recommendations for the proposed information collection within 30 days via reginfo.gov and previously published the information-collection notice in the Federal Register to obtain comments (60 days previously). The PRA section includes an overview of type of collection, title (I-485, Supplement A, Supplement J), affected public, estimated respondents and burden hours, and estimated annual total hour and cost burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of public charge inadmissibility (§212.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the scope: §§212.20–212.23 address the public charge ground of inadmissibility under section 212(a)(4) of the INA and apply to applicants for admission or adjustment of status unless exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the alien requesting the immigration benefit or classification has been exempted from section 212(a)(4) as listed in §212.23(a), the provisions apply to an applicant for admission or adjustment to lawful permanent resident status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Likely at any time to become a public charge' (§212.21(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines when an alien is 'likely at any time to become a public charge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means likely at any time to become primarily dependent on the government for subsistence, as demonstrated by either the receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Public cash assistance for income maintenance' (§212.21(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies which cash assistance programs count as public cash assistance for income maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (1) Supplemental Security Income (SSI); (2) cash assistance under Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF); and (3) State, Tribal, territorial, or local cash benefit programs for income maintenance (often called 'General Assistance').

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Long-term institutionalization at government expense' (§212.21(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies what qualifies as long-term institutionalization at government expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means government assistance for long-term institutionalization (for Medicaid, limited to institutional services under section 1905(a)) received by a beneficiary, including nursing facility or mental health institution. Does not include imprisonment for conviction of a crime or short-period rehabilitation institutionalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Receipt (of public benefits)' (§212.21(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies when an individual's receipt of public benefits is counted for public-charge purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt occurs when an agency provides either public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense to the individual (where the individual is listed as a beneficiary). An individual's application for a benefit, or approval for future receipt, or benefits received solely on behalf of a third party (including household members), does not constitute receipt for that individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Household' for public-charge analysis (§212.21(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines which persons are included in the alien's household for evidentiary and factor analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Household includes: the alien; spouse if physically residing with alien; if physically residing, the alien's parents, unmarried siblings under 21, and children; individuals listed as dependents on the alien's federal tax return; and any individual who lists the alien as a dependent on their federal tax return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum factors to consider in public-charge determination (§212.22(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider a set of minimum statutory factors when determining likelihood of becoming a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum factors: (i) Age; (ii) Health, as evidenced by immigration medical exam report (DHS will generally defer to such report absent evidence it is incomplete); (iii) Family status (household size); (iv) Assets, resources, and financial status (household income, assets, liabilities — excluding income from public benefits in §212.21(b) and income from illegal activities); and (v) Education and skills (degrees, certifications, licenses, skills obtained through work/education, educational certificates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Affidavit of Support (§212.22(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: How an affidavit of support under section 213A of the INA factors into public-charge determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will favorably consider an Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A, when required under section 212(a)(4)(C) or (D), that meets the requirements of section 213A and 8 CFR part 213a, in making a public charge inadmissibility determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of current and/or past receipt of specified public benefits (§212.22(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider current and past receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization in the totality of the circumstances, with limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will consider amount, duration, and recency of receipt, and for long-term institutionalization, evidence that institutionalization violates federal law (e.g., ADA or Rehabilitation Act). However, current or past receipt of these benefits will not alone be sufficient to determine likely to become a public charge. DHS will NOT consider receipt of, or certification/approval for future receipt of, benefits not referenced in §212.21(b) and (c) — such as SNAP or other nutrition programs, CHIP, Medicaid (other than long-term institutional services under section 1905(a)), housing benefits, benefits related to immunizations or testing for communicable diseases, or other supplemental/special-purpose benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability status limitation (§212.22(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disability alone is insufficient to find an alien likely to become a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A finding that an alien has a disability, as defined by Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, will not alone be a sufficient basis to determine likelihood of becoming a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of the circumstances requirement (§212.22(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations must be based on the totality of an alien's circumstances; no one non-213A factor should be sole criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for lack of a sufficient Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A (if required), no single factor should be the sole criterion. DHS may periodically issue guidance to adjudicators informed by empirical analysis of best-available data to inform assessments of how factors affect likelihood of becoming a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial decisions must articulate consideration of factors (§212.22(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for written denial decisions based on totality of circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every written denial issued by USCIS based on totality of circumstances must reflect consideration of each of the factors listed in §212.22(a) and specifically articulate the reasons for the officer's determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-consideration of benefits received while in exempt immigration categories or under a waiver (§212.22(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits received while in immigration categories exempt from public-charge or while under a waiver are not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will not consider public benefits received during periods when the alien was present in an immigration category exempt from the public charge ground (§212.23(a)), or when the alien received a waiver of public charge inadmissibility (§212.23(c)). DHS also will not consider benefits received by aliens eligible for refugee resettlement assistance and other refugee-available benefits (including services described under section 412(d)(2) provided to an unaccompanied alien child).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from the public charge ground (§212.23(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory or regulatory categories of aliens to whom the public charge ground does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes (non-exhaustive list): refugees at admission and adjustment, asylees at grant and adjustment, Amerasian immigrants (per statute), Afghan and Iraqi interpreters/employees of U.S. Government (per specified statutes), Cuban and Haitian entrants, applicants under Cuban Adjustment Act, NACARA beneficiaries, Haitians under HRIFA, Lautenberg parolees, special immigrant juveniles, registry applicants (entered prior to Jan 1, 1972), certain Temporary Protected Status applicants, specified nonimmigrants (Ambassadors, diplomats, certain foreign officials), C-2 and C-3 nonimmigrants, certain NATO categories, T and U nonimmigrant-related categories, VAWA self-petitioners (subject to paragraph b limitations), qualified aliens under PRWORA section 431(c), certain special statutory adjustment categories, and other categories exempt under law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited exemption and affidavit-of-support requirement (§212.23(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories (paragraphs (a)(18)-(21)) are limitedly exempt but must submit an Affidavit of Support if adjustment is based on employment-based petition requiring such affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aliens described in paragraphs (a)(18) through (21) must submit an Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A if they are applying for adjustment of status based on an employment-based petition that requires such an affidavit under section 212(a)(4)(D) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers of the public charge ground (§212.23(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of aliens who may be authorized a waiver of the public charge ground under statutory or regulatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes applicants for admission as nonimmigrants under section 101(a)(15)(S) (and certain S nonimmigrants applying for adjustment under 245(j)), and any other categories eligible to receive a waiver of the public charge ground of inadmissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge bond invitation and acceptance (§213.1(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When USCIS may invite an alien to submit a public charge bond and when consular officers may request acceptance of such bonds before visa issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in adjudicating adjustment of status USCIS determines alien is inadmissible only under section 212(a)(4) and the application is otherwise approvable, USCIS may invite the alien to submit a public charge bond as condition of approval. USCIS may accept a public charge bond before issuance of an immigrant visa upon request from a U.S. consular officer or presentation of the consular officer's notification; consular officer will set the amount (subject to paragraph (c)) and provide submission instructions; USCIS notifies consular officer upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, amount, and minimum for public charge bonds (§213.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements regarding the form and amount of public charge bonds and receipts, including minimum bond amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All bonds and agreements covering cash deposits must be executed on a form designated by USCIS and be in the sum set by USCIS or consular officer but not less than $1,000. USCIS will provide a receipt on a designated form. All public charge bonds are subject to procedures in 8 CFR 103.6 relating to bond riders, acceptable sureties, cancellation, and breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation and breach of public charge bonds (§103.6(c)(1) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for cancellation of a public charge bond and conditions that constitute breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public charge bond posted for an alien will be cancelled when the alien dies, departs permanently from the United States, or is naturalized, provided the alien did not breach the bond by receiving either public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense prior to death, departure, or naturalization. USCIS may cancel a bond at any time after determining the alien is not likely to become a public charge or to allow substitution. USCIS will review for cancellation following the fifth anniversary of admission or adjustment if Form I-356 is filed; if I-356 is not filed, the bond remains in effect until filed and adjudicated.
